**Test image analysis:**
- Whole tomato shoot held in hand
- Severe wilting, leaf curl, and stem drooping
- Small dark/necrotic spots on leaves
- Bronze-green discoloration throughout
- Distorted growing tips
- General collapse of the upper plant

This pattern (bronzing + spots + distortion + wilt) is characteristic of **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus**. Let me now check reference images across 8 classes to confirm.

This CMV reference (1568049) is extremely similar to the test image (1568051) — same field background, same distorted/curled leaf morphology, same narrow twisted leaves. These appear to be sequential Bugwood images from the same source. Let me verify with more references.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **CMV ref (1568049)**: Near-identical to test image (1568051). Sequential Bugwood IDs, same field background, same filiform/shoestring leaf distortion (narrow, curled, twisted leaves). This is the hallmark symptom of Cucumber Mosaic Virus on tomato.
- **CMV ref (1568053)**: Field overview of same CMV outbreak
- **TSWV refs**: Show ring spots on fruit / severe whole-plant bronzing — not matching
- **Bacterial_Wilt ref**: Shows stem streaming test — not matching
- **Bacterial_Canker ref**: Shows leaf margin necrosis — not matching
- **Early_Blight ref**: Shows concentric ring lesions — not matching
- **Verticillium_Wilt ref**: Shows yellowing/marginal scorch — not matching

The test image shows classic CMV "shoestring" symptom: severe leaf distortion, narrow curled leaves, wilted shoot tips — with an identical Bugwood image sequence to the CMV class references.
